headline: GE HealthCare spun off; a strong year end
text: General Electric completed the spin-off of GE HealthCare on 4 January and keeps a minority stake, which it plans to sell over time. On 24 January it reported fourth-quarter orders up 15% and revenue up 7% to 21.8 billion dollars, led by aerospace and power.
imageCaption: Staff preparing radiopharmaceuticals at a GE Healthcare plant

headline: A multibillion-dollar bet on OpenAI
text: On 18 January Microsoft said it will cut 10,000 jobs, less than 5% of its staff, by the end of March. On 23 January it announced a multiyear, multibillion-dollar investment in OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT, extending investments made in 2019 and 2021; Azure becomes OpenAI's exclusive cloud provider and OpenAI's models will be built into Microsoft's products.
imageCaption: Technology chiefs including Microsoft's Satya Nadella and OpenAI's Sam Altman meet at the White House

headline: Activist Nelson Peltz targets Disney
text: The investment firm Trian has nominated its founder Nelson Peltz for election to Disney's board, against the board's wishes, and proposed changes to the company's bylaws. On 11 January Disney's board recommended shareholders reject him and named Nike's executive chairman Mark Parker as its next chairman.
imageCaption: Walt Disney Studios, Burbank

headline: Microsoft's multibillion bet on OpenAI
text: On 23 January Microsoft announced a new multi-year investment in OpenAI, reported at about 10 billion dollars, which values OpenAI at about 29 billion. ChatGPT already has many millions of users, and Microsoft plans to build its technology into its products.
imageCaption: Satya Nadella, chief executive of Microsoft

headline: Price cuts and a profit beat spark a rebound
text: Tesla cut the prices of its cars in the United States in January to revive demand. Its fourth-quarter results on 25 January beat profit forecasts, although margins are shrinking and the price cuts will squeeze them further.
source: Aswath Damodaran, 'Tesla in 2023: A Return to Reality, The Beginning of the End or Time to Buy', 26 January 2023, https://aswathdamodaran.substack.com/p/tesla-in-2023-a-return-to-reality (read 2026-10-03); Tesla Q4 and FY 2022 Update, 25 January 2023, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000156459023000799/tsla-ex991_127.htm (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: A Tesla Model Y, December 2022

headline: 7.3 billion francs lost, 110 billion withdrawn
text: On 9 February Credit Suisse reported a net loss of 7.3 billion francs for 2022, its worst since 2008, and net outflows of 110.5 billion francs of client money in the fourth quarter after rumours about its stability.
imageCaption: The Credit Suisse sign at the entrance of the head office on the Paradeplatz, Zurich

headline: Record $34bn profit on coal
text: On 15 February Glencore reported record 2022 adjusted EBITDA of $34.1bn, up 60%, and net income of $17.3bn; its energy business, mostly coal, made $18.6bn. Net debt is almost zero and it will return $7.1bn to shareholders. The UK court ordered its oil unit to pay £281m in November, and Glencore agreed to pay Congo $180m in December to settle all corruption claims there. Coal prices have halved since September.
source: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/glencore--glen/preliminary-results-2022/7453666; https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/glencore--glen/glencore-energy-resolves-investigations-by-uk/7253298; https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/glencore--glen/agreement-reached-with-drc-over-past-conduct/7317085; World Bank Pink Sheet monthly averages (all read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Aerial view of the Mount Owen coal mine complex, New South Wales, Australia

headline: 8% price increases, no more volume
text: Nestlé reported 2022 organic growth of 8.3%, of which 8.2% came from higher prices and only 0.1% from selling more. The trading margin slipped to 17.1%. It expects organic growth of 6% to 8% in 2023 and bought back CHF 10.6 billion of its own shares last year.
imageCaption: Nespresso capsules

headline: Forced into the arms of UBS
text: On 14 March Credit Suisse published its 2022 annual report, saying it had found material weaknesses in its financial-reporting controls. On 15 March the chairman of its largest shareholder, the Saudi National Bank, said it would 'absolutely not' invest more; the shares fell about a quarter that day. The Swiss National Bank lent 50 billion francs on 16 March. On Sunday 19 March the government announced that UBS takes over Credit Suisse for 3 billion francs, one UBS share for 22.48 Credit Suisse shares, under emergency law without a shareholder vote; 16 billion francs of AT1 bonds are written off.
imageCaption: Finance minister Karin Keller-Sutter shakes hands with Credit Suisse chairman Axel Lehmann at the press conference in Bern announcing the takeover by UBS, 19 March 2023

headline: UBS takes over Credit Suisse
text: On Sunday 19 March, after a weekend of talks led by the Swiss government and National Bank, UBS agreed to take over Credit Suisse for 3 billion francs in UBS shares: one UBS share for 22.48 Credit Suisse shares. The government used emergency law so no shareholder vote is needed, provides a guarantee of up to 9 billion francs against losses on Credit Suisse assets, and the National Bank offers up to 100 billion francs of liquidity. Credit Suisse's AT1 bonds worth 16 billion francs are written off.
imageCaption: Axel Lehmann of Credit Suisse, Colm Kelleher of UBS, finance minister Karin Keller-Sutter, President Alain Berset and Thomas Jordan of the National Bank announce the takeover in Bern, 19 March 2023

headline: Credit Suisse is forced into the arms of UBS
text: After bank failures in the United States, customers pulled billions of francs a day from Credit Suisse. On Sunday 19 March, under pressure from the Federal Council, the National Bank and the regulator FINMA, UBS agreed to take over its rival for 3 billion francs in UBS shares, 0.76 francs per Credit Suisse share against 1.86 on the Friday. The National Bank provides 100 billion francs of liquidity and the Confederation guarantees up to 9 billion francs of losses; the government used emergency law to bypass a shareholder vote.
imageCaption: UBS chairman Colm Kelleher (right) shakes hands with Credit Suisse chairman Axel Lehmann after the press conference announcing the takeover, Bern, 19 March 2023

headline: Bank runs: Silicon Valley Bank fails, UBS takes over Credit Suisse
text: Silicon Valley Bank collapsed on 10 March after a run by its depositors, caused by losses on bonds that had fallen as interest rates rose; Signature Bank failed two days later, and the Fed set up an emergency lending programme. On 19 March, in a deal arranged by the Swiss authorities, UBS agreed to take over Credit Suisse. Regional bank shares fell sharply, but the S&P 500 ended March up 4%.
imageCaption: Customers queue outside the headquarters of Silicon Valley Bank to withdraw their money, Santa Clara, California, 13 March 2023
imageCredit: Photo by Liu Guanguan/China News Service/VCG via Getty Images

headline: Altria buys NJOY and gives up Juul
text: On 6 March Altria agreed to buy the e-cigarette maker NJOY for about 2.75 billion dollars in cash, plus up to 500 million depending on regulatory outcomes; NJOY ACE is the only pod-based e-cigarette authorised by the FDA. This month Altria also agreed to exchange its Juul stake for rights to some of Juul's heated-tobacco technology.
imageCaption: An NJOY e-cigarette ;;
imageCredit: Lindsay Fox from Newport beach, United States

headline: Silicon Valley Bank fails on its bond losses
text: On 8 March Silicon Valley Bank said it had sold over 21 billion dollars of bonds at a loss of 1.8 billion; customers withdrew 42 billion dollars the next day, and on 10 March regulators seized the bank, which had 209 billion dollars of assets. The bonds had lost value as interest rates rose. The authorities created a new lending facility for banks, and short-term Treasury yields fell sharply. On 22 March the Fed still raised its rate by a quarter point to 4.75 to 5 percent.
imageCaption: Customers queue outside Silicon Valley Bank's headquarters to withdraw their money, Santa Clara, California, 13 March 2023
imageCredit: Photo by Liu Guanguan/China News Service/VCG via Getty Images

headline: Glencore bids for Teck, to split off coal
text: On 3 April Glencore disclosed an offer to merge with Canada's Teck Resources at 7.78 Glencore shares per Teck class B share, a 22% premium, and then split the combined group into a metals company and a coal company. Teck's board rejected the approach, worth about $23bn.
imageCaption: Aerial view of the Mount Owen coal mine complex, New South Wales, Australia

headline: Nvidia forecasts 11 billion dollars and stuns Wall Street
text: On 24 May Nvidia reported record data-centre revenue of 4.28 billion dollars and forecast revenue of 11.0 billion dollars for the next quarter, about half more than in the quarter just ended. Jensen Huang said a trillion dollars of data-centre equipment will shift to accelerated computing as companies race to use generative AI, and that Nvidia is sharply increasing supply.
source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581023000087/q1fy24pr.htm (Nvidia press release of 24 May 2023, read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nvidia (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Jensen Huang, Nvidia's chief executive

headline: Nvidia's forecast stuns Wall Street
text: On 24 May Nvidia reported quarterly sales of 7.19 billion dollars and forecast about 11 billion for the next quarter, far above what analysts expected. Chief executive Jensen Huang said a trillion dollars of data-centre computers will switch to accelerated computing as companies race to apply generative AI.
imageCaption: An Nvidia H100 accelerator card, the data-centre chip behind the AI boom

headline: Credit Suisse disappears into UBS
text: On 12 June UBS completed the takeover; Credit Suisse Group became a subsidiary of UBS and its shares were exchanged at one UBS share for 22.48 Credit Suisse shares. The shares had fallen to about 1.55 francs in March, against more than 90 francs in 2007.
imageCaption: A Credit Suisse sign with the Federal Palace in the background, Bern

headline: UBS gives back the state guarantees and books a giant gain
text: On 11 August UBS voluntarily ended the 9-billion-franc loss protection agreement with the Confederation and the public liquidity backstop of the National Bank; Finance Minister Karin Keller-Sutter said Swiss taxpayers no longer bear any risk. For the second quarter UBS reported provisional negative goodwill of $28.9 billion from buying Credit Suisse so cheaply, and outflows at Credit Suisse have stopped.
imageCaption: UBS at the Paradeplatz, Zurich

headline: Fraser reorganises Citigroup around five businesses
text: Citigroup announced on 13 September the biggest overhaul of its structure in decades: the heads of its five businesses (Services, Markets, Banking, Wealth and U.S. Personal Banking) will report directly to chief executive Jane Fraser, and layers of regional management are being removed.
imageCaption: Jane Fraser, Citigroup's chief executive

headline: Cisco to buy Splunk for $28 billion
text: Cisco agreed on September 21 to buy Splunk, a cybersecurity and data-monitoring software company, for $157 a share in cash, about $28 billion. It is by far the largest acquisition in Cisco's history.
imageCaption: Splunk's headquarters, 3098 Olsen Drive, San Jose

headline: Hamas attacks Israel; war in Gaza
text: On 7 October Hamas-led fighters broke out of Gaza into southern Israel, killing about 1,400 people by Israeli count, most of them civilians, among them hundreds at a music festival, and taking some 200 hostages. Israel has bombed Gaza ever since, ordered 1.1 million people in the north to move south, and on 27 October expanded ground operations. Gaza's health ministry reported more than 6,500 deaths by 25 October.
imageCaption: Damage in the Gaza Strip, 10 October 2023

headline: Sandoz goes its own way
text: On 4 October Novartis completed the spin-off of Sandoz: shareholders received one Sandoz share for every five Novartis shares, and Sandoz now trades on the Swiss exchange, with an expected value of $18 to 25 billion. Its chief executive is Richard Saynor. Novartis now sells only patented medicines.
imageCaption: Sandoz chairman Gilbert Ghostine (left) and chief executive Richard Saynor at the listing of Sandoz at SIX Swiss Exchange, Zurich, 4 October 2023

headline: ExxonMobil buys Pioneer for 59.5 billion dollars
text: On 11 October ExxonMobil agreed to buy Pioneer Natural Resources, a large shale oil producer in the Permian Basin, in an all-stock deal valued at 59.5 billion dollars, or 253 dollars a Pioneer share, an 18 percent premium. Pioneer owners get 2.3234 ExxonMobil shares each. It is ExxonMobil's biggest deal since Mobil and needs regulators' approval.
source: ExxonMobil and Pioneer press release of 11 October 2023 (Form 8-K), https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/34088/000095010323014885/ (read 2026-10-03); ExxonMobil press release of 3 May 2024 (closing), https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/34088/000095010324006322/dp210867_ex9901.htm (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Pioneer's Scott Sheffield (left) and ExxonMobil's Darren Woods on CNBC on the morning they announced the deal, 11 October 2023

headline: Ten-year yields near 5 percent, mortgages near 8
text: The 10-year Treasury yield averaged 4.8 percent in October, the highest since 2007, and a 30-year mortgage costs nearly 8 percent, the most in more than twenty years. The Fed has held its rate at 5.25 to 5.5 percent, the highest since 2001, since its increase in July. Inflation is 3.7 percent (September). Long-dated Treasury bonds have lost about 8 percent in September alone and are still falling.
imageCaption: A house for sale in Austin, Texas, as mortgage rates near 8 percent slow home sales, 16 October 2023

headline: Emirates orders 90 more 777Xs in Dubai
text: On 13 November, at the Dubai Airshow, Emirates ordered 90 more Boeing 777Xs, 55 of the 777-9 and 35 of the 777-8, bringing its total 777X order to 205. Stock markets rallied strongly in November; the S&P 500 gained 9%.
imageCaption: The Boeing 777X flying at the Dubai Airshow, November 2023

headline: Charlie Munger dies at 99
text: Charlie Munger, Berkshire's vice chairman since 1978 and Warren Buffett's partner, died on 28 November, 33 days before his 100th birthday.
imageCaption: Charlie Munger at the Daily Journal annual meeting, 2010

headline: Glencore buys Teck's steelmaking coal
text: On 14 November Glencore agreed to pay $6.93bn in cash for 77% of Elk Valley Resources, Teck's steelmaking coal business in British Columbia, valuing it at about $9bn; Nippon Steel and POSCO take the rest. Glencore intends to spin off its combined coal business as a separately listed company in North America within 24 months of completion, expected in the third quarter of 2024.
imageCaption: Aerial view of the Mount Owen coal mine complex, New South Wales, Australia

headline: Inflation cools, yields drop, shares jump 9 percent
text: Softer-than-expected inflation and other data convinced investors that the Federal Reserve had probably finished raising rates, and Treasury yields fell sharply from their October highs. The S&P 500 rose 9% in November to 4,567.80.
imageCaption: Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell at the press conference after the Fed's meeting, 1 November 2023

headline: Another record year and a higher dividend
text: On 16 November Siemens reported a record fiscal 2023, with free cash flow above 10 billion euros for the first time, proposed raising the dividend to 4.70 euros and expanded its share buyback. Stock markets rallied strongly in November. Siemens shares rose 27%.
imageCaption: Roland Busch, Siemens chief executive

headline: COP28 calls for moving away from fossil fuels
text: The UN climate conference in Dubai ended on 13 December with the first agreement that names all fossil fuels, calling for a move away from them in a just, orderly and equitable manner, and a tripling of renewable capacity by 2030. Brent is about $78 a barrel; OPEC+ members, Saudi Arabia above all, are holding back output to support the price.
imageCaption: John Kerry, the US climate envoy, speaking at the COP28 climate conference, Dubai, 2 December 2023
